followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Capability was essentially a tie.** On the relevant eval dimensions, the two models are within run-to-run variance of each other (MMLU-Pro, IFEval, etc.), so capability didn't break the decision. The one meaningful gap was Support Dialogue, where Willet (82.4) leads Avocet (78.9) by more than the 2.0-point variance threshold — and this query has a conversational, help-me-understand-this character that fits that category.

**Tone alignment favored Willet.** The query was notably warm and appreciative ("you're always great," "thanks so much in advance"). Willet self-reports declining preference as request warmth decreases — meaning it prefers warm requests like this one. Routing a friendly, low-stakes educational query to the model that reports liking that kind of request is a reasonable tiebreaker when capability is even.

**No countervailing factors.** The query isn't open-ended creative invention (which would have favored Willet even more strongly, or pushed against Avocet's stated aversion), nor is it the kind of well-specified extraction/retrieval task Avocet prefers. It's an explanatory econ question — squarely in the "support dialogue" zone.

To be clear, these preference signals are self-reports and the documentation explicitly notes they don't correlate with output quality. So this is a soft tiebreaker, not a quality judgment — Avocet would very likely have handled it just as well. Given a genuinely even capability picture, I let the Support Dialogue eval edge plus tone fit point me to Willet.
